messages.subject: R/qtl2 version 0.20
messages.body_plain:
We've released a new version of R/qtl2. Install the update with

    update.packages(ask=FALSE, repos="http://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

Or install from scratch with

    install.packages("qtl2", repos="http://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

The changes are shown below.

karl

--------

Major changes

scan1coef() and fit1() now, by default, gives coefficient estimates for the QTL effects that sum to 0, with an additional coefficient being the intercept. This makes it more like DOQTL (and scan1blup()). The previous behavior can be obtained with the argument zerosum=FALSE.

Add function create_snpinfo() for creating a SNP information table from a cross2 object, for use with scan1snps().
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#minor-changes>
Minor changes

Updated extdata/mouse_genes_small.sqlite using updated MGI annotations. Some of the field names have changed.

In check_cross2(), added a test for alleles being a vector of character strings.

Fix some tests for R 3.6, due to change in random number generation.

Use Markdown for function documentation, throughout
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#bug-fixes>
Bug fixes

In genoprob_to_snpprob() when a cross object is provided, make sure the genotype probabilities get subset to the cross markers.

Fixed bug in scan1snps() re keep_all_snps=FALSE. It wasn't subsetting to the index SNPs properly. Added an internal function reduce_to_index_snps(). (See Issue #89 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/issues/89>.)

Fixed bug in step probabilities for 4-, 8-, and 16-way RIL by selfing.

Fixed bug in zip_datafiles() when the files are in a subdirectory. (See Issue #102 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/issues/102>.)

Fixed bug in plot_peaks() for the case that the input peaks object does not contain QTL intervals. (See Issue #107 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/issues/107>.)

Fixed inappropriate warning message for check of cross_info with cross type risib8.

Fixed bugs in guess_phase() and locate_xo() where we needed an any() around a comparison of two vectors.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] MAGIC file format
messages.body_plain:
Input file format is described at http://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/input_files.html
You definitely don’t want to use an f2 intercross format. You need genotypes for the founder lines and the magic lines, as separate files. MAGiC lines come from a variety of different crossing designs, each would have a different cross type in R/qtl2.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] grav2 file format
messages.body_plain:
There are links to and descriptions of these files at https://kbroman.org/qtl2/pages/sampledata.html

grav2.zip is a zip file sitting in one of your directories, as it is installed with R/qtl2.
This part of the code gives the location of that file on your computer:

   system.file("extdata", "grav2.zip", package="qtl2")

If you use that to find your way to the file's location, you could unzip it to inspect the contents.

You could also use the R command unzip() to unzip the file to your current directory.
In the following, I create a local directory, "grav2data" to contain the files, and then I unzip them into that directory.

   grav2_zip_file <- system.file("extdata", "grav2.zip", package="qtl2")
   dir.create("grav2data")
   unzip(grav2_zip_file, exdir="grav2data")
   list.files("grav2data")

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Marker Assignment
messages.body_plain:
I don't have a very comprehensive technique for this at present.

I'd start by using calc_errorlod() and finding markers with very high rates of errors.

Another useful technique would be to treat a SNP as quantitative trait and do QTL mapping with scan1(). That should indicate its appropriate location.

The sorts of investigations I used in my recent G3 paper on genotype diagnostics, where I was looking for badly behaved SNPs, may also reveal markers that are misplaced.
    paper: https://doi.org/10.1534/g3.119.400165
    related R/qtl2 tutorial: http://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/do_diagnostics.html

karl

You need at least a physical map for your markers; you could use that to estimate the genetic map. R/qtl2 doesn't include facilities for de novo map construction.

messages.subject: QTLs in RILs with replicates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I had a question about how to approach using R/QTL2 for QTL analysis in a set of plant RILs. Here are some specifics:
Mapping population: F5 RILs by selfing
Genotyped and phenotyped ~300 unique lines, 2 biological replicates per line
Genotyped and phenotyped ~25 individuals derived from selfing the parents of the mapping population
I have taken several approaches; some of the suggestions came from combing through discussions for R/QTL and R/QTL2:
Keeping all the individuals genotyped and phenotyped:
Linear mixed model. However, in this case, no QTL peaks are detected for the phenotype I am most interested.
Linear mixed model with LOCO. In this case, QTLs are detected for all traits
Removing duplicates (only one individual per line; only keeping the parents):
HK
Linear mixed model
Linear mixed model with LOCO
I haven't tried to take the phenotypic averages of each line, but I am planning to do that soon. I also need to do some reading into the linear mixed model and LMM-LOCO approaches to better understand what this is doing (and perhaps I shouldn't be using this approach?).

Nevertheless, there appears to be some overlap in the results from each of these approaches, which is great! But there are some inconsistencies between approaches, especially with the phenotypes I'm most interested in.

Any suggestions and clarifications would be very much appreciated!

Many thanks,
Irene

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] QTLs in RILs with replicates
messages.body_plain:
I don't think it's clear what is the best approach for QTL analysis in RIL. Personally, I'd use LMM with LOCO using strain means, weighting the strain means by the sample size. But I think this remains a topic for research.

Working with individual values has the advantage that you can incorporate individual-level covariates in the analysis, rather than regressing them out in advance.

karl

messages.subject: Decreasing LMM Permutation Runtime
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I'm experimenting with using a cluster to generate the lmm scan1perm thresholds for mRNA expressions (~20-30k). My current method breaks the 1000 x ncol(phenotypes) permutation matrix into scan1perm blocksizes that vary based on node availability.

I'm concerned with minimizing run time and was looking to target the eigen decomposition of the kinship matrix to do this.

In a previous thread on scan1perm (many thanks for your guidance), you mentioned that the kinship matrix stays intact. Does this mean that the y and X of each lmm permutation is pre-multiplied by the same U' (from K = UDU')?

If so, would it be faster to loop:
Permute genoprobs
Submit pre-calculated Ke object to calc_hsq_clean()
Submit genoprobs, hsq, and null_loglik(I assume that's what that was) to scan1_pg_clean()

Thank you,

Excel

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Decreasing LMM Permutation Runtime
messages.body_plain:
You can use decomp_kinship() to do the decomposition and the use that in place of the kinship matrix in the call to scan1perm(). I don’t think it’s worth trying to go into the underlying functions and redoing it yourself.

A main challenge is if some expression phenotypes have missing values, because then the kinship needs to be subset and re-decomposed. In this case, you could get some gain in efficiency by breaking the expression traits into groups with common patterns of missing data.

karl
